questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to quantify cost/benefit for a hybrid CRDT-based collaboration system across regions, balancing latency, bandwidth, and privacy.

## Key Concepts

- CRDT convergence cost on-device
- Hybrid architecture: edge vs central index
- Data residency and privacy/compliance implications
- Inter-region delta traffic and network costs
- Rollout strategy, drift detection, and maintenance

## Code Example

```typescript
// Minimal CRDT merge skeleton for text lines
type Line = string
function merge(linesA: Line[], linesB: Line[]): Line[] {
  const out = new Set<string>([...linesA, ...linesB])
  return Array.from(out)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you model break-even with stochastic user load and regional variance?
- What metrics would you monitor in production to validate the CBA assumptions?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to quantify cost and risk of privacy-preserving ML in production, balancing technical constraints with business impact.

## Key Concepts
- Federated learning cost modeling (CAPEX/OPEX breakdown)
- Differential privacy utility trade-offs (ε parameter tuning)
- Multi-region deployment economics
- Business metrics translation (accuracy → GMV/SLA)
- Risk mitigation strategies for edge ML

## Technical Parameters
- Model architecture: LSTM + attention heads (45MB)
- Training frequency: Hourly updates, 100 rounds/epoch
- DP configuration: ε=0.5 per update, δ=1e-5, Gaussian noise σ=2.1
- Network: 1Gbps regional backbone, <50ms intra-region latency
- Hardware: Jetson AGX Xavier (32 TOPS, 32GB RAM, 512GB SSD)

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you implement federated averaging across regions with different data distributions?
- What monitoring dashboard would detect drift in privacy-utility trade-offs?
- How would GDPR right-to-deletion be implemented in federated context?

- On-device ML for keyboards and latency budgets
- Privacy-by-design and optional cloud feedback
- Incremental rollout, drift/maintenance, break-even horizon
- Measurement and instrumentation considerations

```javascript
// Example energy estimation snippet (illustrative)
function estimateEnergyPerKeystroke(modelSizeKB, keystrokesPerHour, cpuPowerW){
  // simplified estimate

}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you design A/B tests to validate cloud feedback benefits vs on-device updates?
- What regulatory concerns could apply with typing data and how would you address them?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assess ability to translate a feature into a cost-benefit plan with edge constraints and privacy governance. Requires concrete data footprints, compute budgeting, and clear go/no-go criteria.

## Key Concepts

- Edge compute and energy budgeting
- Data retention and delta-sync costs
- Privacy/compliance considerations (PII, anonymization)
- Break-even calculation and go/no-go thresholds

## Code Example

```javascript
function breakEven(monthlyCost, uplift) {
  if (uplift <= 0) return Infinity;
  return Math.ceil(monthlyCost / uplift);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would changing data-retention periods alter cost estimates?
- How would you handle false positives impacting maintenance costs and user trust?
